scope: Seven-day real-world-only BWM and DROID monitor v3
summary: A new detached monitor now watches the restarted seven-day WorldArena/BWM queue and the real DROID SVO calibration queue while preserving explicit simulator exclusions.
evidence: The restarted BWM waiter is alive on a800-1 as PID 2604840 with maximum_wait_seconds=604800 and a verified waiting-official-bwm heartbeat.
The DROID calibration waiter remains alive on a800-1 as PID 1442133.
The first v3 monitor heartbeat records both jobs as running and both successors as not started.
The BWM postprocessor remains a fixed argv successor and can launch only after a WORKING result.json.
lessons: Resource-wait recovery must change the timeout policy, preserve the old attempt, and use a new immutable directory.
Monitoring all active real-world queues prevents a single terminal event from ending campaign visibility.
limitations: Both scientific jobs are still waiting for strictly available GPUs.
Action swaps remain diagnostic without physically executed counterfactual branches.
next_actions: Continue 120-second capacity/job polling for up to seven days.
Automatically postprocess BWM only after both matched inference arms complete.
Append terminal DROID calibration and BWM outcomes to the ledger.
